pharm: Intravenous iron (polynuclear iron(III)-hydroxide sucrose complex); hematinic
quick: 100 mg IV per dialysis session (HDD-CKD); 200 mg IV x5 over 14 days (NDD-CKD); 300/300/400 mg IV (PDD-CKD)
Not relevant (IV); do not co-administer oral iron simultaneously
Treat IDA; first-trimester data limited; severe reactions may cause fetal bradycardia
Present in milk; reported compatible; monitor infant for GI upset
Indicated for IDA in CKD; no specific renal dose reduction

summary: Iron sucrose is an intravenous iron replacement product (a polynuclear iron(III)-hydroxide in sucrose complex) indicated for treating iron deficiency anemia in patients with chronic kidney disease. It is given by slow IV injection or infusion only, with dosing individualized by CKD population (hemodialysis-dependent, non-dialysis-dependent, peritoneal dialysis-dependent, and pediatric maintenance). Serious, sometimes fatal, hypersensitivity and hypotension can occur, so patients must be observed during and for at least 30 minutes after each dose. Periodic monitoring of iron studies is required to avoid iron overload.
indications: Treatment of iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD)

dosage.d: 100 mg elemental iron per dialysis session; usual total course 1000 mg (10 sessions)
dosage.t: Each consecutive hemodialysis session, given early in the session (generally within the first hour); may repeat course if iron deficiency recurs
dosage.n: Give undiluted as slow IV injection over 2-5 min, or diluted in up to 100 mL 0.9% NaCl over at least 15 min

dosage.d: 200 mg elemental iron per dose on 5 different occasions over a 14-day period (cumulative 1000 mg)
dosage.t: 5 occasions across 14 days; may repeat if iron deficiency recurs
dosage.n: Undiluted slow IV injection over 2-5 min or in up to 100 mL 0.9% NaCl over 15 min; limited experience with 500 mg in up to 250 mL over 3.5-4 h on Day 1 and Day 14

dosage.d: Two 300 mg infusions then one 400 mg infusion (3 divided doses within a 28-day period)
dosage.t: 300 mg over 1.5 h on Day 1 and Day 15 (14 days apart), then 400 mg over 2.5 h on Day 29 (14 days later); may repeat if iron deficiency recurs
dosage.n: Dilute each dose in a maximum of 250 mL 0.9% NaCl by slow IV infusion

dosage.d: 0.5 mg/kg, not to exceed 100 mg per dose
dosage.t: Every 2 weeks for 12 weeks; may repeat if necessary
dosage.n: Undiluted slow IV over 5 min, or diluted in 0.9% NaCl to 1-2 mg/mL over 5-60 min; do not dilute below 1 mg/mL. Iron replacement dosing not established

dosage.c: Pediatric (>=2 yr) NDD-CKD or PDD-CKD maintenance (on erythropoietin)
dosage.d: 0.5 mg/kg, not to exceed 100 mg per dose
dosage.t: Every 4 weeks for 12 weeks; may repeat if necessary
dosage.n: Undiluted slow IV over 5 min, or diluted in 0.9% NaCl to 1-2 mg/mL over 5-60 min; do not dilute below 1 mg/mL. Iron replacement dosing not established

admin: Administer intravenously only, by slow injection or infusion; never give by other routes
Dose is expressed in mg of elemental iron; each mL contains 20 mg elemental iron
Observe patient for hypersensitivity and hypotension during and for at least 30 minutes after each dose, until clinically stable
Only administer where personnel and therapies for treating serious hypersensitivity reactions are immediately available
When diluting, use only 0.9% NaCl; do not dilute to concentrations below 1 mg/mL
Do not mix with other medications or add to parenteral nutrition solutions
Ensure stable IV access to avoid extravasation; inspect visually for particulates and discoloration before use; discard unused portion
moa: Iron sucrose is an aqueous complex of polynuclear iron(III)-hydroxide in sucrose. After IV administration it dissociates into iron and sucrose; the iron is transported as a complex with transferrin to target cells including erythroid precursors, where it is incorporated into hemoglobin as the cells mature into red blood cells, replenishing iron stores and supporting erythropoiesis.

relative: Iron overload (do not administer to patients with evidence of iron overload)
Prior history of reactions to parenteral iron products
monitor: Signs/symptoms of hypersensitivity during and after each dose (at least 30 minutes)
Blood pressure for hypotension during and following each administration
Hematologic and iron parameters (hemoglobin, hematocrit, ferritin, transferrin saturation) periodically

preg: Published studies of IV iron sucrose after the first trimester have not shown adverse maternal or fetal outcomes; first-trimester data are insufficient to assess risk of major birth defects or miscarriage. Untreated IDA in pregnancy carries maternal and fetal risks (post-partum anemia, preterm delivery, low birth weight) and should be treated. Severe maternal reactions causing circulatory failure (severe hypotension, shock) may cause fetal bradycardia, especially in the second and third trimesters. Animal studies at doses up to the maximum recommended human dose showed no fetal harm.
lact: Iron sucrose is present in human milk; published reports following 100-300 mg IV doses have not reported adverse reactions in breastfed infants, and there are no data on effects on milk production. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and potential effects on the infant. Monitor breastfed infants for gastrointestinal toxicity (constipation, diarrhea).
renal: Indicated specifically for iron deficiency anemia in patients with chronic kidney disease (HDD-CKD, NDD-CKD, PDD-CKD, and pediatric maintenance); dosing is defined by CKD population rather than by renal function-based reduction. Iron sucrose is not removed by high-efficiency or high-flux dialysis membranes.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is provided. Excessive parenteral iron can accumulate in storage sites (including liver) causing iatrogenic hemosiderosis; avoid in iron overload and use caution in elderly patients who may have decreased hepatic function.

moderate: Oral iron preparations: iron sucrose may reduce absorption of concomitantly administered oral iron; avoid simultaneous administration
interactions.food: No clinically significant food interactions (IV administration).
interactions.diagnostics: Transferrin saturation (TSAT) rises rapidly after IV dosing; do not measure serum iron for at least 48 hours after a dose to avoid falsely elevated values.

serious: Serious hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylactic-type reactions
rare: Acute myocardial ischemia/infarction in the context of a hypersensitivity reaction
emergency: Anaphylaxis / shock with hypotension, loss of consciousness, or collapse

monitoring: Transferrin saturation (TSAT) - do not measure serum iron for at least 48 hours after dosing
Signs and symptoms of hypersensitivity during and for at least 30 minutes after each dose
Blood pressure for hypotension during and after each administration
Breastfed infants for GI toxicity if mother is treated
counsel: This medication is given only into a vein by a healthcare professional
Report any prior reactions to IV iron products before treatment
Report symptoms of an allergic reaction during or after the dose: rash, itching, dizziness, light-headedness, swelling, or breathing problems
Tell your team if you feel faint, dizzy, or develop low blood pressure symptoms after a dose
You will need periodic blood tests to monitor iron levels and avoid getting too much iron
Do not take oral iron at the same time as your iron sucrose infusions unless advised
pk: Significant rises in serum iron/ferritin; hemoglobin response over weeks
Iron distributes mainly in blood; pediatric Cmax ~8545 mcg/dL (7 mg/kg dose)
Iron component ~6 hours in healthy adults (~8 hours in pediatric NDD-CKD)
Iron taken up by liver, spleen, and bone marrow (irreversible trapping compartment)
Store at 20-25C (68-77F), excursions 15-30C; do not freeze; no preservatives
pearls: Dose is always expressed as elemental iron; each mL = 20 mg elemental iron (vials: 50 mg/2.5 mL, 100 mg/5 mL, 200 mg/10 mL)
HDD-CKD usual total course is 1000 mg given as 100 mg over 10 consecutive dialysis sessions; may repeat if deficiency recurs
Most reactions occur within 30 minutes of completing the infusion; slowing the infusion rate may alleviate symptoms
TSAT rises rapidly after dosing - wait at least 48 hours before checking serum iron to avoid spurious results
Iron sucrose is not dialyzable (high-efficiency/high-flux membranes), so dialysis does not remove it
Do not give to patients with iron overload; only administer where anaphylaxis treatment is immediately available
missed: Iron sucrose is given on a scheduled basis by a clinician (per dialysis session or on set days). If a dose is missed, resume the schedule as directed by the treating team; the full treatment course may be extended or repeated if iron deficiency recurs. Do not double doses.
overdose: No human overdosage data exist. Excessive dosing can cause iron accumulation and hemosiderosis. Iron sucrose is not dialyzable through high-efficiency or high-flux membranes, so dialysis is ineffective for removal. Avoid administration in patients with iron overload; manage supportively and monitor iron parameters (do not measure serum iron for at least 48 hours after a dose).
